title: Make finding-registry violation predicates executable defect checks
description:
Decomposed out of eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6 (PR #476) 2026-07-26 under the churn stop
rule. Review of f75acb2 found this as a NEW DEFECT CLASS.

DEFECT: the violation queryId merely SELECTS a row, after which every finding
runs the same baseline-existence join. Wrong field values, missing branches,
incorrect resets and lifecycle errors are never evaluated, and
`expectedAfterRepair` is unused entirely. So a "violation query" proves only
that the row's baseline members still exist — which is not a defect check.

CONSEQUENCE: the registry cannot detect recurrence. A repaired defect that
regresses in a different form leaves the baseline intact and the query green.
That defeats the zero-repeat certification at eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4, which is the
registry's whole purpose.

SCOPE: give each finding an executable predicate that evaluates the ACTUAL
defect condition against the committed pack — wrong value, missing branch,
absent alternative, incorrect reset, broken lifecycle, unsupported provenance —
and make `expectedAfterRepair` operative: 'empty' rows must go empty when
repaired and fail if they do not; 'stable' rows must keep their membership.

NOT IN SCOPE HERE: deriving membership for prose-scoped rows (that is
eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7) and capability target identity (the sibling bead created
alongside this one).

DEPENDENCY NOTE: clause-level predicates likely need the clause IR from
eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1, which is itself under design reopening. Record any row whose
predicate cannot be written yet rather than writing a shape-only stand-in.
acceptance_criteria:
• Every finding row carries a predicate that evaluates its actual defect condition, not a baseline-existence join.
• expectedAfterRepair is operative and tested in both directions.
• A repaired-then-regressed defect in a different form is detected by its predicate.
• Rows whose predicate cannot yet be written are explicitly recorded and block closure rather than carrying a shape-only stand-in.
